Extract the keywords of documents

Source: R/keywords.R
keywords.Rd

keywords() extracts the keywords of each document: the words and short phrases that best express what it is about. Embedding-based keyword extraction compares the meaning of each candidate phrase with the meaning of the whole document, and a phrase whose embedding is close to the document's embedding summarizes it well; because picking the closest phrases alone tends to return near-synonyms, the selection also rewards phrases that differ from those already chosen, by maximal marginal relevance (Carbonell and Goldstein 1998), as in KeyBERT (Grootendorst 2020).

The candidates are the words and phrases of up to ngrams consecutive words of each document after stop words are removed; the documents and the candidates are encoded with the same model, and up to n keywords per document are selected. The result is a data frame with one row per keyword. keywords() describes single documents; to describe topics, use terms(), which compares the words of a topic with those of the other topics.

keywords() encodes text, so it needs a downloaded model.

Usage

keywords(
  text,
  model = NULL,
  n = 10L,
  ngrams = 2L,
  topic_diversity = 0.3,
  stop_words = default_stop_words(),
  min_token_length = 3L,
  batch_size = 32L
)

Arguments

text

Documents: a character vector. Names, if any, are carried into document_name.

model

The encoder: a model from load_model(), a pinned model name, or NULL (default) for the default model.

n

Maximum number of keywords per document (default 10).

ngrams

Maximum length of a candidate phrase, in words (default 2).

topic_diversity

Trade-off between relevance and diversity, in [0, 1): 0 ranks by similarity to the document alone, and larger values penalize candidates similar to those already chosen (default 0.3).

stop_words

Words excluded from the candidates; default stop_words().

min_token_length

Minimum length of a candidate word, in characters (default 3).

batch_size

Texts encoded per model call (default 32).

Value

A base data frame with one row per keyword and columns document_id, document_name, rank, keyword, and topic_similarity (the cosine similarity between the keyword and its document).

Conditions

An error of class sbert_no_terms when no candidate is left after stop words and short words are removed; the errors of load_model() and encode().

References

Carbonell, J. and Goldstein, J. (1998). The use of MMR, diversity-based reranking for reordering documents and producing summaries. Proceedings of SIGIR 1998, 335–336. doi:10.1145/290941.291025

Grootendorst, M. (2020). KeyBERT: Minimal keyword extraction with BERT. doi:10.5281/zenodo.4461265

See also

terms() for the terms of topics; stop_words(); model_download() to download a model.

Examples

# Pinned models that can encode the text
models()
#>                                    model dimensions max_tokens      languages
#> 1                       all-MiniLM-L6-v2        384        256        English
#> 2                      all-MiniLM-L12-v2        384        128        English
#> 3                paraphrase-MiniLM-L3-v2        384        128        English
#> 4              multi-qa-MiniLM-L6-cos-v1        384        512        English
#> 5  paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2        384        128  50+ languages
#> 6                      all-mpnet-base-v2        768        384        English
#> 7  paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2        768        128  50+ languages
#> 8                      bge-small-en-v1.5        384        512        English
#> 9                       bge-base-en-v1.5        768        512        English
#> 10                 multilingual-e5-small        384        512 100+ languages

#> 12           jina-embeddings-v2-small-en        512       8192        English
